extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (also patent applicants and practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Form-paragraph and procedural guidance for examining patent claims (primarily indefiniteness under 35 U.S.C. 112 and related rejection grounds), including specific categories of indefinite language, new matter, duplicate claims, disclaimers, foreign filing issues, final rejections, and related examiner actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure To Particularly Point Out And Distinctly Claim (Indefinite)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which applicant regards as the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection must be preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103.2 and followed by one or more applicable form paragraphs (7.34.02 - 7.34.11) or supply a full explanation of the deficiency. Whenever possible, identify particular terms/limitations rendering the claim indefinite and explain why. If one of ordinary skill can determine the scope, this rejection is not appropriate. See MPEP §§ 2171-2174.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.02 Terminology Used Inconsistent with Accepted Meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant defines a claim term contrary to its ordinary meaning, the written description must clearly redefine the term and set forth the uncommon definition so as to put one reasonably skilled in the art on notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite Process Control Corp. v. HydReclaim Corp. Provide the applicant's assigned meaning (bracket 3) and the accepted meaning (bracket 4). Support accepted meaning with appropriate references (e.g., textbook/dictionary). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01 and used only where specification does not clearly redefine the term.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.03 Relative Term - Term of Degree Rendering Claim Indefinite
rubrics_metrics.description: A relative term of degree appearing in a claim that is not defined by the claim or the specification, and for which one of ordinary skill in the art would not be reasonably apprised of scope, renders the claim indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain which parameter/quantity/limitation in the claim is rendered indefinite (bracket 3). This paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.04 Broader Range/Limitation And Narrow Range/Limitation in Same Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad range or limitation together with a narrower range/limitation falling within the broad range in the same claim is considered indefinite because the metes and bounds are unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert broader range/limitation (bracket 2) and the narrow range/limitation (bracket 3) and note whether the narrow language is exemplary or required. Cite Ex parte Wu and related decisions. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.05 Lack of Antecedent Basis in the Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim recites a limitation without sufficient antecedent basis in the claim, rendering the scope indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert limitation lacking antecedent basis (bracket 2) and identify location in the claim (bracket 3). Use only in aggravated situations where lack of antecedent basis makes claim scope indeterminate. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.06 Use Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that provide for the use of something but do not set forth any steps involved in the method/process are unclear and indefinite; a mere recitation of a use without active steps may not be a proper process claim under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert what is being used (bracket 2). See MPEP § 2173.05(q) and authorities (Ex parte Dunki, Clinical Products v. Brenner). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.07 Claims Are a Literal Translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that are narrative, indefinite, and appear to be literal translations from a foreign document (with grammatical/idiomatic errors) fail to conform to current U.S. practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when claims are poorly written/translated. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.08 Indefinite Claim Language: 'For Example'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'for example' in a claim renders the claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following the phrase are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite MPEP § 2173.05(d). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.09 Indefinite Claim Language: 'Or The Like'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'or the like' renders claims indefinite because it includes elements not actually disclosed, making scope unascertainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite MPEP § 2173.05(d). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.10 Indefinite Claim Language: 'Such As'
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'such as' renders a claim indefinite because it is unclear whether the limitations following are part of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite MPEP § 2173.05(d). Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.11 Modifier of 'Means' Lacks Function
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'means' clause preceded by words that do not convey a function is indefinite under 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, because equivalents cannot be determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words preceding 'means' must convey a function (e.g., 'latch means' conveys 'latching'). If the phrase can be restated as 'means for _____' and still make sense, it is definite. Cite Ex parte Klumb. Must be preceded by form paragraph 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.12 Essential Steps Omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as incomplete for omitting essential steps; omission amounts to a gap between steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recite the omitted steps (bracket 2) and give rationale for considering the omitted steps critical or essential. Preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.13 Essential Elements Omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as incomplete for omitting essential elements; omission amounts to a gap between elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recite omitted elements (bracket 2) and provide rationale for considering them critical or essential. Preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.14 Essential Cooperative Relationships Omitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, for omitting essential structural cooperative relationships of elements, creating gaps in necessary structural connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recite omitted structural cooperative relationships (bracket 2) and give rationale for their criticality. Preceded by form paragraph 7.30.02 or 7.103.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.34.15 Rejection Under 35 U.S.C. 112, Pro Se
rubrics_metrics.description: For pro se applicants: claim(s) are narrative, replete with indefinite/functional/operational language; structure must be clearly and positively specified, organized to present a complete operative device, and claims must be in one-sentence form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to explain deficiencies in pro se-filed claims; note format of cited patents as examples. Preceded by applicable form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.35 Rejection, 35 U.S.C. 112, 2nd Paragraph - Omnibus Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim rejected as indefinite because it fails to point out what is included or excluded by the claim language; the claim is an 'omnibus' type (e.g., 'A device substantially as shown and described').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precede rejection with form paragraph 7.30.02. No further explanation necessary; see MPEP § 1302.04(b) for cancellation by examiner's amendment upon allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.35.01 Trademark or Trade Name as a Limitation in the Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim containing a trademark/trade name as a limitation does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, because trademarks identify source, not the goods, creating uncertain claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert trademark/trade name (bracket 2) and specify the material/product identified (bracket 3). Cite Ex parte Simpson (218 USPQ 1020). Preceded by applicable form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 706.03(k) Duplicate Claims — Examiner Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When two claims are duplicates or so close in content that both cover the same thing, it is proper after allowing one claim to object to the other as a substantial duplicate under 37 CFR 1.75.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give applicant opportunity to correct problem. Use form paragraphs 7.05.05 (warning) or 7.05.06 (objection) where appropriate. If duplicate claims are present, use 7.05.05 to warn; if claims are objectionable, use 7.05.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.05.05 Duplicate Claims, Warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant is advised that should claim [1] be found allowable, claim [2] will be objected to under 37 CFR 1.75 as being a substantial duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use whenever two claims are substantial duplicates but not allowable; gives applicant opportunity to correct and avoid later objection. If claims become allowable, use 7.05.06 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.05.06 Duplicate Claims, Objection
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] objected under 37 CFR 1.75 as being a substantial duplicate of claim [2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when duplicate claims are not allowable. See MPEP § 804 for double patenting rejections where inventions are not patentable over each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 706.03(o) New Matter — Examiner Alert
rubrics_metrics.description: New matter (subject matter not disclosed in the original application) added after filing may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 132; examples include adding unsupported subject matter, adding specific percentages/compounds after a broader disclosure, or omitting a method step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2163.06-2163.07(b), § 608.04(c), In re Wertheim. Examiner must detect new matter in amended cases and object under 35 U.S.C. 132; use form paragraph 7.28 to object to new matter added to the specification. If new matter added affects claims, also use 7.31.01 (112, first paragraph) for claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.28 Objection to New Matter Added to Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment filed is objected to under 35 U.S.C. 132 because it introduces new matter into the disclosure; identify added material not supported by original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant required to cancel new matter in reply. Use form paragraph 14.22.01 in reissue applications. In bracket 2, identify new matter by page/line/drawing and provide explanation addressing any applicant statements that subject matter was described on filing; include unresolved questions raising doubt as to possession at time of filing. If new matter added to claims, reject under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph (7.31.01) rather than this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 706.03(s) Foreign Filing Without License (35 U.S.C. 182-185)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a foreign patent application before six months after U.S. filing without a license may result in abandonment or barring of the U.S. patent; unauthorized foreign filing can forfeit claims against the U.S. government and invalidate a U.S. patent if license not procured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners who learn of earlier foreign filing should refer the application to Licensing and Review Section of the TC work group 3640. Pending investigation, application may be returned to the TC for prosecution on the merits; Licensing and Review will request transfer if action under 35 U.S.C. 185 is necessary. See statutory provisions, conditions for retroactive licenses, and definitions of 'application.'

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 706.03(u) Disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be rejected on the ground that applicant has disclaimed the subject matter (e.g., failure to present claims for interference, to copy a claim from a patent when suggested, or failure to respond/appeal to rejections of copied claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection on disclaimer applies to all claims not patentably distinct from disclaimed subject matter as well as directly involved claims. Use Form Paragraphs 7.48 and 7.49 for such rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.48 Failure To Present Claims for Interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. [2] based on claim [3] of Patent No. [4] for failure to present claims or take necessary steps for interference after notification, constituting a disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only after applicant was notified that interference proceedings must be instituted and applicant refused to copy the claims. Insert statutory citation (e.g., 102(g)) and patent number. If rejection is under 103(a), include the examiner’s basis for obviousness. Note that interferences may include obvious variants; see MPEP § 2306.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.49 Rejection, Disclaimer, Failure To Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim stand finally disposed of for failure to reply to or appeal from the examiner's rejection of such claim(s) presented for interference within specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite 37 CFR 1.661 and 1.663. Use where applicant failed to prosecute/appeal in interference context.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 706.03(v) After Interference or Public Use Proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes of interferences or public use proceedings may be grounds for rejection; upon termination of related proceedings, notify the Board to resume interference prosecution where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2363.03 and 37 CFR 1.292. If needed, send notice to Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences to resume proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 706.03(w) Res Judicata
rubrics_metrics.description: Res judicata may be a proper ground for rejection when an earlier decision by the Board or reviewing court exists and there is no opportunity for further court review of that decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply only when earlier decision was of Board or reviewing court and no further court review available. Often accompany rejections on prior art; consider same prior art in continuing applications. Numerous case citations where res judicata was sustained or reversed are provided (e.g., In re Freeman, In re Fried).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 706.03(x) Reissue — Scope and Bar
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 251 forbids granting a reissue enlarging the scope of the claims of the original patent unless applied for within two years of grant; reissue claims broader than original may be rejected as barred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation applies to any claim broader in any respect. Reissue applications by assignee that enlarge scope may be rejected, but courts have allowed corrective actions in some circumstances (In re Bennett). Defective reissue oath can be ground for rejecting all claims in reissue application. See MPEP Chapter 1400.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 706.04 Rejection of Previously Allowed Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable shall thereafter be rejected only after the proposed rejection is submitted to the primary examiner for consideration and approval; full faith should be given to prior examiner's actions absent clear error or new art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 7.50 to indicate withdraw of allowability and identify newly discovered references. Great care in authorizing rejection; do not adopt entirely new approach or new search merely hoping to find new grounds. See Ex parte Grier and Amgen v. Hoechst Marion Roussel guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.50 Claims Previously Allowed, Now Rejected, New Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowability of claim [1] is withdrawn in view of newly discovered references [2]; rejections based on newly cited references follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert newly discovered references (bracket 2). Any such action requires signature of a Primary Examiner. See MPEP § 1004.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 706.07 Final Rejection — Requirements for Finality
rubrics_metrics.description: On second or subsequent examination, the rejection or other action may be made final; the examiner must repeat/state all grounds of rejection and clearly state reasons supporting them. Reply to final rejection limits applicant's reply (appeal or limited amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before final rejection, develop a clear issue between examiner and applicant. Final rejection should reiterate outstanding grounds of record with sufficient development for applicant to judge appeal. If a single previous action contains complete statement, final may refer to it but should rebut applicant's arguments. Conclude final rejection with Form Paragraph 7.39. See 37 CFR 1.113 and related MPEP guidance on fairness, extension of time policy, and avoidance of premature final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.39 Action Is Final
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph concluding that the action is made final and reminding applicant of the extension of time policy as set forth in 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to notify applicant that the action is final and provide procedural reminder about time extensions under the rules.
